Stage 2 assigns A+: the three-night format merits actively finding room during a Tokyo stay, while three available dates and no premiere, farewell or final-performance claim make S unnecessary. events.subtitle: New Year Special 2027 — three contrasting ensembles across three nights
events.category: Master drummer residency / modern Japanese jazz / rotating ensembles
lineup: January 2: Takeo Moriyama — drums; Tetsuro Kawashima — tenor saxophone; Takashi Sugawa — cello; Kosuke Sakai — bass
January 3: Takeo Moriyama — drums; Takumi Nakayama — alto saxophone; Mikiko Nagatake — piano; Takashi Sugawa — bass
January 4: Takeo Moriyama — drums; Yoshiaki Sato — accordion; Reiko Yamamoto — vibraphone; Nobumasa Tanaka — piano
events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents Takeo Moriyama's New Year Special 2027 from January 2 through January 4. Doors open at 17:30 and music starts at 18:00 each night. The three date-specific lineups move from tenor saxophone, cello and bass on January 2, to alto saxophone, piano and bass on January 3, and accordion, vibraphone and piano on January 4. PIT INN lists ¥5,500 including tax and one drink for each performance; ticket sales and reservations open December 1 at 11:00. In the venue's program text, Moriyama reflects on having played jazz drums for sixty years.

en.why_it_matters: Moriyama is not repeating one working quartet for three nights. He changes the music's center of gravity each evening: tenor saxophone against cello and bass; alto saxophone with piano and bass; then accordion, vibraphone and piano without a listed bassist. That rotating architecture gives a master drummer's sixty-year perspective three genuinely different frames instead of turning the engagement into a generic anniversary set.
en.trip_verdict: If a Tokyo stay overlaps the New Year run, actively make room for one evening and choose by instrumentation: January 2 for the cello-led low end, January 3 for a classic piano-quartet frame, or January 4 for the unusual accordion-vibraphone-piano palette. Three available dates leave useful flexibility.

es.why_it_matters: Moriyama no repite un mismo cuarteto de trabajo durante tres noches. Cada fecha cambia el centro de gravedad: saxo tenor frente a violonchelo y bajo; saxo alto con piano y bajo; y luego acordeón, vibráfono y piano sin bajista anunciado. Esa arquitectura rotativa coloca sesenta años de perspectiva de un maestro de la batería en tres marcos realmente distintos, en vez de convertir el ciclo en un aniversario genérico.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Tokio coincide con el ciclo de Año Nuevo, busca espacio para una noche y elige por instrumentación: el 2 de enero por el registro grave con violonchelo, el 3 por el marco clásico de cuarteto con piano, o el 4 por la paleta inusual de acordeón, vibráfono y piano. Las tres fechas ofrecen flexibilidad útil.
